module: Main jbeam vehicle loader: orchestrates all the steps that transform the .jbeam files and the chosen configuration into a vehicle data "bundle" (vdata) ready for the physics. Order: file reading (jbeam/io), part selection by the slot system, variable application, part unification, table schema, section merging, link and cid resolution, nodes/beams, wheels, groups, scaling, option default values, optimization, interaction. Then loadBundle creates engine-side: events, plates, colors, initial node positions, meshes, ropes, materials, faces, mirrors. Runs in both VMs (GE and vehicle, vmType). A modder mostly uses it to read the loaded config or to use the hooks onJbeamLoadingPhase1/2.
notes: Beam type constants (defined in C, do not modify): NORMAL 0, ANISOTROPIC 1, BOUNDED 2, PRESSURED 3, LBEAM 4, BROKEN 5, HYDRO 6, SUPPORT 7.

Default values applied to vehicle.options if absent: beamSpring = defaultBeamSpring (4300000), beamDeform = defaultBeamDeform (220000), beamDamp = defaultBeamDamp (580), beamStrength = defaultBeamStrength (math.huge), nodeWeight = defaultNodeWeight (25).

Emitted hooks (extensions.hook): onJbeamLoadingPhase1(loadingProgress, objID, vehicle, unifyJournal, vehicleConfig, vars) after nodes/beams and before wheels; onJbeamLoadingPhase2(...) before optimization.

occupantSlots and the camera are only handled in the GE VM (vmType == 'game'). loadBundle creates the visible objects only on the GE side (if the vehicle object is found), otherwise sets props and flexbodies to {}.
A bundle cache (key = SHA256 of the folders + config) avoids reloading an identical vehicle; emptied by onFileChanged. The bundle is stored encoded and decoded on each reuse.

The config parameter additionalVehicleData.indestructible makes all beams other than wheels/torsionbars/rails infinitely strong (beamStrength = huge) and removes triggers and actionsEnabled (code marked TODO: REMOVE TEST CODE).
A gameEngineExtensions section of the parts allows automatically loading GE extensions (name = true, or name = {args} calls onVehicleExtensionLoaded(objID, args) on the extension).
If the command-line argument -debugVehicleLoading is present, vehicleDebug_*.json files are written in the vehicle folder.
M.materials and M.materialsMap (from particles.getMaterialsParticlesTable()) are exported fields missing from the automatic list.
Minor bug: loadJbeam returns nil without closing the profilerPush when findParts fails (return before profilerPopEvent).

data.desc: Empty table created at initialization (not filled in this file).

materialsMap.desc: Materials mapping table (second return value of the same function).

_noSerialize.desc: true: the module is not serialized during a VM reload.

loadVehicleStage1.desc: Vehicle loading entry point: normalizes the folder (leading and trailing slash), adds /vehicles/common/, consults the cache, calls loadJbeam then loadBundle and tracks progress in the LoadingManager (GE side).

returns.desc: Bundle {id, vehicleDirectory, directoriesLoaded, vdata, config, mainPartName, ioCtx}; nil on failure.

loadJbeam.desc: Loads and assembles in memory all the vehicle's jbeam data (parts, variables, tables, links, cid, wheels, groups, optimization) without touching the 3D objects.

vehicleDirectories.desc: Jbeam folders (the first is the vehicle folder).

returns.desc: Vehicle bundle; nil if a step fails.

loadJbeamOnlyConfig.desc: Like loadJbeam but only chooses the parts: returns the completed configuration (model, mainPartName, mainPartPath, partsTree).

returns.desc: Completed vehicleConfig; nil if there is no main part.

loadBundle.desc: Creates engine-side everything that depends on the vehicle object: input events, plates, colors, paints, initial node positions and collisions, reference nodes, meshes, visual ropes, materials, occupant faces, mirrors, and loads the extensions listed in gameEngineExtensions. Without a vehicle object (vehicle VM), sets props and flexbodies to {}.

cacheVehicleBundleForEditor.desc: If the editor cache is enabled, stores an encoded copy of the bundle (temporarily adding editorTransform to the props) for the editor.

vehicleObj.desc: Engine vehicle object (to read the props' transforms).

getCachedVehicleBundle.desc: Returns a decoded copy of the bundle cached for the editor.

setEditorCacheEnabled.desc: Enables or disables the editor cache; disabling empties it.

onFileChanged.desc: Hook called when a file changes: empties the bundle cache and the editor cache.
